one_liner: Mid-to-senior federal buyer for ICE: plan, solicit, negotiate, award and manage complex supply and service contracts under federal acquisition rules.
fit_summary: This GS-12 role requires a FAC-C (Professional) or equivalent contracting certification at the time of application, plus one year of GS-11-level contracting work such as cost/price analysis and solicitation preparation. Nothing on file shows Daniel has either. Daniel's consulting work at IEM for government clients and strong people skills fit the customer-service and negotiation competencies, but they cannot substitute for the certification selective placement factor.
eligibility: Open to the public and to federal career-transition (ICTAP/CTAP) applicants under Direct Hire Authority, so no federal status is needed.
Selective placement factor: you must hold a FAC-C (Levels I-III or Professional), DAWIA Contracting, or DoD Contracting Professional certification and submit a copy with the application.
Basic requirement: a bachelor's degree in any field, or 24 semester hours in business-related fields, verified by transcripts you must upload.
Specialized experience: one year at the GS-11 equivalent doing cost/price analysis, determining contract type, preparing solicitations and evaluation criteria, and developing negotiation strategies.
You must pass the USA Hire online assessment cut score and a pre-employment drug test.
strategy: Before investing time, confirm whether you hold any FAC-C, DAWIA, or DoD contracting certification. If you don't, this posting is effectively closed to you, so skip it.

If you lack certification, target GS-1102 entry-level or intern roles at GS-5/7/9, or DHS and ICE acquisition development programs, and start the FAC-C (Professional) training through FAI.gov to build toward roles like this one.

If IEM work involved proposals, pricing, or task orders, describe it specifically: the contract vehicles, your role in cost volumes or pricing, and your hours per week. Screeners will not assume experience.
Keep the resume to two pages, with month/year dates and hours per week for each job, and put the contracting-specific bullets first.
Gather your transcripts and certification certificate early. The window runs October 19 to November 2, 2026, and missing documents mean disqualification.
Answer the questionnaire honestly. Overstated claims will be checked against your resume and can get you removed from consideration.
resume_bullets: Supported [number] government-client engagements at IEM in [emergency management/disaster recovery] by [preparing cost/pricing inputs or proposal sections], working with [client agency] on contracts valued at [$ amount]; [hours/week].
Reviewed [client] requirements and helped draft [statements of work/evaluation criteria] for [type of procurement], meeting [deadline or outcome you can verify].
Coordinated with [number] client and subcontractor stakeholders to track contract performance and deliverables on [project], resolving [type of issue] before [milestone].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would perform a price analysis for a services requirement when there is limited competition.
How do you decide the appropriate contract type for a complex requirement?
Describe a negotiation where you had to balance a customer's needs against compliance rules.
Tell us about a time you managed a post-award problem with a contractor's performance.
watch_outs: The contracting certification requirement is a hard screen-out, and nothing on file suggests you have it.
There is no promotion potential above GS-12, and the duty locations are Irving TX, Orlando FL, or Washington DC, so the DC option is a commute from Manassas.
Consulting experience on the contractor side counts only if it clearly involved acquisition tasks at GS-11 complexity.
The application window is only two weeks (October 19 to November 2, 2026).
